title: Gaming & VR Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Comprehensive checklist to protect your privacy while gaming and using VR. Secure your gaming data, prevent tracking, and stay safe online.
intro: Gaming platforms and VR headsets collect vast amounts of personal data including gameplay habits, biometric information, voice recordings, and social interactions. This checklist helps you secure your gaming privacy and protect sensitive information from data brokers and advertisers.

items.task: Review and adjust privacy settings on all gaming platforms
items.why: Gaming platforms collect extensive data about your gameplay, purchases, and social interactions that can be shared with third parties.
items.howTo: Go to privacy settings on Steam, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, Epic Games, etc. Disable data sharing for marketing, limit friend visibility, and turn off activity tracking where possible.

items.task: Disable voice chat recording and data collection
items.why: Voice recordings can be stored indefinitely and used for advertising profiling or shared with law enforcement without your knowledge.
items.howTo: In platform settings, turn off voice data collection, disable voice-to-text features, and opt out of voice recording for game improvement purposes.

items.task: Limit social features and friend recommendations
items.why: Gaming platforms scan your contacts and social media to suggest friends, potentially exposing your real identity to strangers.
items.howTo: Disable contact syncing, turn off friend suggestions based on external accounts, and set your profile to private or friends-only visibility.

items.task: Opt out of targeted advertising and data sharing
items.why: Gaming companies sell your behavioral data to advertisers and data brokers, creating detailed profiles of your interests and habits.
items.howTo: Navigate to advertising preferences in account settings. Disable personalized ads, opt out of data sharing with partners, and turn off cross-platform tracking.

items.why: VR headsets collect biometric data including eye tracking, hand movements, and room mapping that can reveal sensitive personal information.
items.howTo: Access privacy settings on Oculus/Meta Quest, HTC Vive, or other VR platforms. Disable biometric data collection, turn off room scanning, and limit sensor data sharing.

items.task: Review VR app permissions and data access
items.why: VR apps can access cameras, microphones, location data, and movement patterns, potentially creating detailed surveillance profiles.
items.howTo: Check permissions for each VR app individually. Revoke unnecessary access to cameras, microphones, and location services. Only grant permissions essential for app functionality.

items.task: Secure VR account with strong authentication
items.why: VR accounts contain sensitive biometric and behavioral data that could be devastating if compromised by hackers.
items.howTo: Enable two-factor authentication on your VR platform account. Use a unique, strong password and consider using a password manager for additional security.

items.task: Limit VR social interactions and content sharing
items.why: VR social features can expose your real-world location, physical appearance, and personal behaviors to strangers and companies.
items.howTo: Set VR social features to private, disable automatic content sharing, turn off location sharing in VR apps, and be cautious about what you say in VR environments.

items.task: Use privacy-focused browsers for gaming websites
items.why: Gaming websites track your browsing behavior and can link your web activity to your gaming accounts for advertising purposes.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser when visiting gaming websites, forums, or stores. This blocks trackers and prevents cross-site data collection while browsing gaming content.

items.task: Create separate email addresses for gaming accounts
items.why: Using your main email for gaming exposes you to data breaches and links your gaming activity to your real identity across platforms.
items.howTo: Create dedicated email addresses for different gaming platforms. Use email aliases or services like ProtonMail to keep gaming accounts separate from personal communications.

items.task: Regularly review and delete gaming data
items.why: Gaming platforms accumulate years of personal data that increases your privacy risk and can be accessed by unauthorized parties.
items.howTo: Periodically delete old gameplay recordings, chat logs, and stored payment information. Use data deletion tools provided by platforms or submit formal deletion requests.

items.why: Children's gaming data receives special legal protection, but default settings often allow extensive data collection that violates their privacy.
items.howTo: Set up parental controls on all gaming platforms, disable data collection for children's accounts, turn off social features, and regularly review their gaming activity and privacy settings.
